meta.notes: Continuous atmospheric phenomena. Each modulator independently evaluates strength from live signals and applies deltas to the directive after the Almanac picks its base. Authored Halo 2026-05-20 (Phase 6).

modulators.label: Cold front passage
modulators.description: A falling barometer over 3 hours warms the sun cast, cools the sky low-band, and lifts wind scale — the visible texture of frontal passage. Canonical ADR example.

modulators.label: Severe storm — tornado green
modulators.description: Eerie yellow-green light when thunderstorm WMO codes coincide with late-afternoon hours and heavy precip — the optical signature of hail-dense supercells filtering low-angle sun through a green-tinted scattering layer. Canonical ADR example.

modulators.label: Wildfire smoke
modulators.description: When direct sun is disproportionately attenuated vs diffuse (smoke / heavy aerosol), the sun goes orange, the dome takes a brown-amber wash, and overall intensity falls. Driver inverts direct/diffuse ratio — clean air has ratio ~0.7+; thick smoke pulls it under 0.4.

modulators.label: Pre-storm gold
modulators.description: The deep golden cast that lands when low-angle sun rakes underneath a heavy cloud deck. Bell curves on cloudCover (mid-heavy) and sunElevationDeg (low but above horizon) compose to fire only in the narrow window where both hold.

modulators.label: About to rain
modulators.description: Falling pressure + high humidity + heavy cloud cover compose to the muted, slightly-cooler, slightly-flatter light of the half hour before a rain begins. Sun dims, ambient floor lifts (cloud-diffused), dome top cools.

modulators.label: Fog burn-off
modulators.description: Mid-morning hours with mid-band cloud cover (the bell catches the clearing arc) light the dome with a warm, hazy diffusion — sun softens, horizon goes pale-warm, the air reads moist.

modulators.label: Summer heat haze
modulators.description: Hot midday hours with measurable direct/diffuse haze flatten the dome cool, blanch the sun toward white, slow the wind. Distinct from wildfire smoke (which goes orange); heat haze stays neutral-grey-blue.
